subject: Subprocessor boundary and data-use redline — product/security decision needed
body:
---Message 1 of 4---
From: Elliot Price <elliot@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Cc: Claire Lloyd <claire.lloyd@clovertech.com>, Maria Ortega <maria.ortega@klgates.com>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Subprocessor boundary and data-use redline — product/security decision needed

Team —

CloverTech returned a set of DPA redlines this morning that narrow our allowed subprocessor behaviors and add an explicit prohibition on any telemetry or derived analytics being exported off their tenant scope. Key asks attached (see clovertech_redline_v3.docx) and highlighted below:

- No telemetry subprocessor may persist request-level metadata beyond 7 days.
- No analytics exports containing derived labels or embeddings are allowed without separate consent.
- Runtime caching is limited to in-memory KV only; persistent cache use must be disclosed and approved.

Legal (K&L Gates) is pushing for a hard commitment to the above. CLA notes they want these as contract obligations rather than product promises.

Questions for Product/Security:
1) Can Redwood enforce a 7-day TTL on all telemetry and request-level logs per-customer in our hosted offering? If not, what's the realistic implementable limit and the engineering effort?
2) Is it feasible to block derived-embedding exports for a tenant without a big perf/regression hit (i.e., can we stop embeddings routing to analytics subprocessors while keeping inference latency SLOs)?
3) Does our current subprocessor list contain any vendors that persist telemetry longer than 7 days? If so, which ones and are there contract remedies?

Next steps I'm proposing:
- Olga to flag immediate security/product blockers and propose temp carveouts.
- Stephanie to estimate time-to-implement and potential SLO impact.
- Priyom to capture anything that needs a formal procurement/contract workaround.

We need an internal decision within 48 hours to avoid escalation. CloverTech is asking for an answer by EOD Wed.

Thanks,
Elliot
Elliot Price
Director, Account Strategy — Redwood Inference
---

---Message 2 of 4---
From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
To: Elliot Price <elliot@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Cc: Claire Lloyd <claire.lloyd@clovertech.com>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Subprocessor boundary and data-use redline — product/security decision needed

Elliot —

Thanks for surfacing. Quick notes from a security perspective: we can probably scope telemetry retention per-tenant in our ingestion path, but there are some caveats:

- Our central observability (TelemetryHub Inc.) currently stores request traces and debug logs for 30 days for backend ops. Shortening to 7 days is operationally doable but will remove debug window; we'd want an exemption process for escalations.
- Embeddings exports are performed in two places: (a) model-serving runtime (real-time embeddings used for retrieval) and (b) analytics pipeline (batch jobs that create analytics indexes). We can gate (b) — i.e., prevent analytics pipeline pulls — without touching (a). That should satisfy the "no analytics exports" ask if CloverTech agrees that runtime embeddings used for retrieval are not "exports."
- Persistent KV cache vendors: CacheOps (our edge cache partner) persists snapshots for failover. We need to confirm snapshot retention.

I've attached a draft subprocessor matrix (subprocessor_matrix_v2.xlsx) with current retention windows and which systems touch embeddings.

Proposed temporary stance to tell CloverTech:
- We can sign a DPA commitment to a 7-day retention on telemetry for customer-controlled logs in hosted mode, excluding platform-level backend traces required for stability and security, for which we propose a 30-day operational window with an escalation path.
- We will block analytics pipeline exports of derived labels/embeddings for the tenant by configuration (no code change for retrieval path).

This is contingent on Product confirming retrieval vs analytics definition and on Procurement confirming if CacheOps can reduce snapshot TTL.

Olga
Olga Petrov
Senior Security Engineer
---

---Message 3 of 4---
From: Maria Ortega <maria.ortega@klgates.com>
To: Elliot Price <elliot@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Cc: Claire Lloyd <claire.lloyd@clovertech.com>
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 08:20:00 -0400
Subject: RE: Subprocessor boundary and data-use redline — product/security decision needed

Elliot/Team —

Appreciate the quick reply and the matrix. From counsel perspective, CloverTech's redline_text (attached) will need either: (A) a firm contractual commitment with narrow technical exceptions enumerated in the DPA, or (B) a signed addendum that memorializes an operational carveout (e.g., 30-day backend logs for platform security) and an explicit escalation path for incident investigations.

Important for contracting: the language as currently proposed is absolute ("no telemetry exports"). We recommend one of the following compromise phrasings to avoid broad operational risk while meeting customer demand:

- Option 1 (preferred): "Redwood will not permit analytics exports of customer-derived embeddings or labels to third-party analytics processors for the customer tenant. Platform operational telemetry necessary to maintain security, stability, and fraud detection for the service is exempt and will be retained up to 30 days. Any snapshot persistence for disaster recovery will be limited to encrypted at-rest storage with a maximum retention of 30 days and will not be used for analytics indexing without customer consent."

- Option 2: Same as Option 1 but with a defined escalation review within 48 hours for any request to access operational telemetry beyond 7 days.

We can prepare a redline file with either Option 1 or Option 2. If Product can confirm the retrieval vs analytics split and Procurement can confirm CacheOps TTL change, we can accept Option 1 into the DPA.

I'll also include a DocuSign readiness link when legal marks which option to incorporate.

Thanks,
Maria Ortega
Associate — K&L Gates
---

---Message 4 of 4---
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
To: Elliot Price <elliot@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Cc: Claire Lloyd <claire.lloyd@clovertech.com>, Maria Ortega <maria.ortega@klgates.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Jun 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Subprocessor boundary and data-use redline — product/security decision needed

Quick product/ops readout and recommendation: 

- Retrieval vs analytics: confirmed. Retrieval embeddings (used inline by the runtime for similarity/search) are not considered "analytics exports" in our internal taxonomy. The analytics pipeline is a separate batch downstream job. We can implement a tenant-config boolean to disable all pipeline pulls of embedding artifacts within 3 business days; cost/latency impact is negligible for runtime.
- Telemetry TTL: Changing TelemetryHub's default retention to 7 days for a single tenant requires a config gating plus a small automation (~2 sprints) to ensure alerting windows are adjusted. Risk: reduces debug window; we should offer a short-term paid escalation to extend retention for incidents.
- CacheOps snapshots: Procurement had an initial call — CacheOps can offer a 7-day snapshot TTL for an additional fee; we need procurement to confirm contract amendment lead time (estimate 2 weeks).

Recommendation to accept Maria's Option 1 with a product-side Addendum that: 
1) Declares analytics exports blocked for the tenant (we will toggle pipeline).
2) Exempts platform operational telemetry with the 30-day operational window; we will document the escalation flow for investigations.
3) Notes CacheOps snapshot retention will be reduced to 7 days once contractual amendment is completed; until then, snapshots will remain subject to existing vendor TTL (documented in matrix).

If you all agree, I will:
- Create a short Product ticket (RD-PL-2179) to implement the tenant config to block analytics pipeline pulls (ETA 3 business days).
- Author a short runbook for the operational-exemption escalation path.
- Signal procurement to start the CacheOps amendment.

Elliot — if you want, I can draft the precise product carveout language for legal to paste into the DPA. Recommend we go with Option 1 and then track the CacheOps amendment as a follow-up milestone (deal condition: amendment in 14 days).

Stephanie Nguyen
Product Manager, Redwood Inference
